subject: Nanotechnology
title: What Is Nanotechnology?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is Nanotechnology?.

hook.text: Gold is yellow — until you shrink it to 20 nanometers, when it turns ruby red.

buildup.text: Nanotechnology works at 1 to 100 nanometers — a scale where familiar rules stop applying.

discovery.text: At this size, surface atoms dominate and quantum effects emerge, giving materials new properties.

twist.text: The same atoms behave completely differently just because there are fewer of them packed together.

climax.text: Engineers now design at this scale deliberately — building medicines, chips, and materials atom by atom.

punchline.text: Same atoms, new rules — that is nanotechnology.

quiz.question: Why do nanoscale materials behave differently from bulk materials?
options: They are made of lighter atoms
Surface effects and quantum mechanics dominate at tiny sizes
They are always in a liquid state
